terms.comment: The everyday word for doing a thing with care: looking, reading, keeping, looking after. Cūrā tē dīligenter is Cicero’s “take good care of yourself”. From dīligēns, attentive, careful (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 2.1.30: accūrātē agātur, doctē et dīligenter (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of work done with pains and precision; Lewis & Short gives dīligenter, studiōsē, exquīsītē as its synonyms.

phrases.latin: Fac ita ut jussī. — Faciam. — At dīligenter. — Fīet. — At mātūrē. — Fīet.
phrases.english: Do as I told you. — I will. — Carefully, mind. — It shall be done. — And promptly. — It shall be done.

phrases.latin: tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam. cūrā tē dīligenter. valē.
phrases.english: Let me know when to expect you. Take good care of yourself. Goodbye.

phrases.latin: sed dīligenter intuēre hās nēniās: quantam sub titulīs ūtilitātem reperiēs!
phrases.english: but look closely at these trifles: how much use you will find under their titles!
let it be done with pains, skill and care

sources: Lewis & Short: diligenter · Lewis & Short: diligo · Lewis & Short: accurate · Lewis & Short: accuro
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-terentius, loci-cicero-epistulae, loci-phaedrus), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
